zaf_note: The SARB itself publishes no named list of holders on its current site. Its Shareholder Information page (https://www.resbank.co.za/en/home/about-us/shareholder-information) says it has 'just over 800 shareholders', 2,000,000 issued shares, a 10,000-share cap per holder with associates, one vote per 200 shares for South African residents, and that the 'Shareholders Index Report is a shortened version of the electronic register'; a printed register can be inspected by prior arrangement (otcstf@resbank.co.za). The SARB publication index still lists a 'Shareholder Index Report' published 4 Aug 2022 at /en/home/publications/publication-detail-pages/shareholders-index-report/2022/shareholder_indexreport30april2022 (note: dated 30 April 2022, not 30 June), but that page now returns 'Page not found', so it could not be opened. The SARB Annual Report 2025/26 (https://www.resbank.co.za/content/dam/sarb/publications/reports/annual-reports/2026/sarb-2025-26.pdf, p.24) gives 855 shareholders at 31 March 2026 and names no holders; its 2025 AGM minutes record 46 shareholders present and 7 by proxy. The only SARB-published document naming holders is the 2014 court application on its 'Regularisation of Shareholding' page (https://www.resbank.co.za/content/dam/sarb/publications/shares-correspondence/2015/6633/SARB-Notice-of-motion--Part-1-.pdf): 29 respondents, mostly private individuals and a family trust, each said to hold 5,000-10,000 shares and to exceed the cap together with associates; it states 508,910 shares were held in contravention of the Act and 297,810 by the respondents. On 4 Nov 2016 the High Court (case 88570/2014) ordered respondents 1-11 and 17-28 to sell shares above 10,000 through Investec Securities within two years at not less than R1.55 (https://www.resbank.co.za/content/dam/sarb/publications/shares-correspondence/2015/6633/Judgement-4-November-2016.pdf). These individuals were not added as holders because the holdings are from 2014 and were ordered sold. The named institutional holders already in owners.json (Daily Investor / BusinessTech, citing the 30 June 2022 index) remain unverified against a primary source.

fed_note: These are NOT the top holders of each Reserve Bank. They are the holders found whose own SEC 10-K names the Reserve Bank they hold stock in, with the dollar amount where printed. Per-bank Federal Reserve Bank stock is not available from FFIEC/FDIC: the Call Report puts Federal Reserve Bank stock inside Schedule RC-F item 4 ('Equity investments without readily determinable fair values') together with Federal Home Loan Bank stock and other equities (FFIEC 051 instructions, RC-F, 3-18: https://www.fdic.gov/resources/bankers/call-reports/crinst-051/2018/2018-03-051-rc-f.pdf). FDIC BankFind gives each bank a 'FED' district field, but it cannot be used to assign stock: JPMorgan Chase Bank (FED 04, Columbus OH), Citibank (FED 09, Sioux Falls SD), HSBC Bank USA (FED 05, Tysons VA) and Morgan Stanley Bank (FED 12, Salt Lake City UT) all appear in the NY Fed's own 2018 holder list. Large holding companies report Fed stock in 10-Ks without naming the Reserve Bank, e.g. SEC XBRL tag FederalReserveBankStock: Bank of America $5.4bn (2025-12-31), Wells Fargo $3.5bn (2024-12-31), Charles Schwab $655m, Ally $452m, HSBC USA $437m, Huntington FRB stock $616m (10-K table); these cannot be placed in a district from what was opened. Some XBRL values are clearly mis-tagged (e.g. Southern First Bancshares $181.2m, The Bancorp $1.99bn) and were not used. Dallas and Minneapolis: no filing found that names the Reserve Bank and gives an amount. No FOIA release of a 'Capital Stock Master Report' for any Reserve Bank other than New York was found. Shares and pct are left null because no source states them (Fed stock has $100 par with half paid in, but share counts were not computed).

case_updates.summary_addition: Simić was arrested on 11 January 2006 with Vladimir Zagrađanin, an investigation was ordered, and the NBS Council removed him as vice-governor on 16 January 2006; no indictment, verdict or acquittal was found.
case_updates.source_title: Central Banking, 'Serbian central bank deputy fired' (17 Jan 2006); Vreme (18 Jan 2006)

case_updates.summary_addition: No court outcome for the 2006 abuse-of-office charges against Mullei was found in the sources opened.
case_updates.source_title: Central Banking, 'CBK governor charged with abuse of office'

case_updates.summary_addition: On 26 April 2006 Judge Esenjan Abylkasymov acquitted Sarbanov and four other former finance officials, ruling there was no crime because they 'acted in the interests of state'; the prosecutor's office said it would appeal, and no appeal outcome was found.
case_updates.source_title: Central Banking, 'Kyrgyz's Sarbanov acted in interests of state' (28 Apr 2006)

case_updates.summary_addition: On 29 December 2002 Turkmenistan's Supreme Court sentenced Orazov in absentia to 25 years over alleged involvement in the 25 November 2002 armed attack on President Niyazov, and the People's Council raised it to life imprisonment the next day; Amnesty International called the trial grossly unfair. This conviction is for the alleged attack, not the loan-embezzlement accusation.

On 22 February 2017 prosecutors indicted 18 people in the Corpbank case, including former deputy governors Tsvetan Gounev and Roumen Simeonov for malfeasance in office over failing to exercise control over Corpbank; no verdict was found.
case_updates.source_title: BTA, '18 Persons Charged in Corpbank Case' (22 Feb 2017)

case_updates.summary_addition: The Milan Court of Appeal cut Fazio's Antonveneta sentence from four years to two years and six months on 28 May 2012, and on 28 November 2012 the Court of Cassation (judgment no. 12989, filed 21 March 2013) upheld the appeal ruling, making the conviction final.
case_updates.source_title: FISAC-CGIL, 'Confermata la condanna di Fazio'; Diritto Penale Contemporaneo on Cass. sez. II n. 12989/2013

case_updates.summary_addition: Around 30 January 2025 Ghana's Attorney-General filed notice to withdraw all charges against Asiama in both the uniBank and UT Bank trials; on 22 July 2025 the A-G also filed a nolle prosequi ending the uniBank case against Duffuor and others after recovering over 60% of the funds allegedly lost.
case_updates.source_title: Graphic Online, 'Attorney-General withdraws charges against former Deputy BoG Governor Johnson Asiama' (30 Jan 2025)

case_updates.summary_addition: At the Moscow City Court on 17 April 2007 prosecutors asked for 15 years in a strict-regime colony for Mishin, plus a fraud conviction over an apartment, and 12 years for tax official Oleg Alekseev; the verdict was not found.
No court outcome for the 2012 arrest warrant was found; Shabibi died on 8 January 2022, when the Central Bank of Iraq issued a statement mourning him as a distinguished former governor.
case_updates.source_title: Central Bank of Iraq news release (8 Jan 2022)

case_updates.summary_addition: As of 21 October 2026 the full Sejm vote on bringing Glapiński before the State Tribunal had not taken place; the Sejm Marshal said it would be taken up in the second half of November 2026 (sittings set for 5-6 and 17-19 November).
case_updates.source_title: Super Biznes, 'Trybunał Stanu dla prezesa NBP? Wiemy, kiedy kluczowe głosowanie' (21 Oct 2026)

case_updates.summary_addition: On 13 March 2024 the Hungarian government sent the draft amendment to the central bank act back for further consultation instead of submitting it to parliament, setting it aside 'at least for now'; a separate 2025 amendment package was proposed, and whether it passed was not checked.
case_updates.source_title: Telex, 'A kormány visszadobta a törvény módosítását...' (14 Mar 2024)
